results.title: India-UAE FTA Talks: Market access, gold quota and data sharing reviewed under CEPA - The Hindu
results.label: yes
results.reason: economy/international_india: Trade data, gold quota, and CEPA framework are key economic indicators.

notes.subject: ir
notes.why_in_news: The Commerce Ministry announced that the joint committee under the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) reviewed market access, gold import quotas, and data sharing to boost economic ties.
notes.fact_box: Bilateral trade between India and UAE exceeded $100 billion in 2024-25, marking a 19.6% increase over 2023-24. The two nations have set a target to reach $100 billion in non-oil and non-precious metal trade by 2030.

prelims_pointers.text: Bilateral trade between India and UAE crossed $100 billion in 2024-25.
Target for non-oil and non-precious metal trade is $100 billion by 2030.
APEDA (Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority) is involved in food safety MoU with UAE.
UAE (United Arab Emirates) is a key trading partner under the CEPA framework.
The committee discussed data sharing and gold Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) allocation.

notes.mains_question: Examine how the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) serves as a catalyst for diversifying India's trade basket beyond traditional commodities.
mains_dimensions: Trade diversification: Shifting focus toward non-oil and non-precious metal sectors to achieve the 2030 target.
Regulatory alignment: Harmonizing food safety standards and pharmaceutical regulations to facilitate smoother bilateral trade.
Transparency in commodities: Transitioning to a competitive bidding process for gold Tariff Rate Quotas (TRQ) to ensure market integrity.

notes.subject: security
notes.why_in_news: BSF IG Aloke Kumar Chakraborty stated that the Ministry of Home Affairs is considering a proposal for a new design of barbed wire fencing along the India-Bangladesh border to replace aging infrastructure.
notes.fact_box: India shares a 4,096 km international border with Bangladesh, with Tripura accounting for 856 km of this stretch. The BSF is currently working to replace old fencing affected by heavy rainfall and wear.

prelims_pointers.text: Tripura's share of the India-Bangladesh border: 856 km
